The layout checklist, scored row by row

The 33-row acceptance checklist run against the INF GSD Limited Edition build — the source of record. Eleven rows pass. Twenty-two fail. Three of the failures are not the build’s fault: those rows cannot be passed by anybody until the checklist itself is corrected.

Build scored: INF GSD Limited Edition · served page Served sha256: 9f819d15c71a…5c57 · matches commit a3b9eae1 Checklist: 2026-11-10-gsd-layout-acceptance-checklist.html Method: headless Chrome over CDP, rendered DOM + screenshots
33 rows scored
11 pass
22 fail

Every row was scored on what a person sees on the screen, never on what the data layer intends. Pass requires every part of the row to be visible, in the place the row puts it. Anything described but not visible, or visible somewhere else, counts as a fail — the same rule the checklist sets.

Before the scorecard: three rows nobody can pass

These are defects in the checklist, not in the build. Fix them and the score gets fairer for both sides.

  1. The rows have no numbers The sign-off table asks for “01.1 – 01.6”, “04.1 – 04.6 × 8”, “05.1 – 05.7” — but no row on the page is numbered. The only place those ids appear is inside the sign-off table itself. To report “row 04.3 failed” you must count from the top of a section, which is exactly how two people end up arguing about which row they meant. One row, one verdict needs one row, one id.
  2. 02.2 does not add up It asks for “Thirteen tiles in total” and then lists Survival 4 + Growth 4 + Founder Freedom 3 + Foundation 3 — fourteen. The build holds fourteen in its data and renders twelve on the screen. Three numbers, one row, and no build can satisfy it until someone picks one.
  3. 06.2 asks for a count that exists nowhere “All 65 metrics defined once.” The build holds 124 metric definitions, the Metric Library prints “59 metrics” in its own heading and “124 metrics” in its own footer, and 118 rows render. 65 is not on the screen, in the data, or in the footer. Either the number is stale or the library has to be cut to it — say which.

One question I would settle first

Rows 05.2 – 05.7 say each brand board “leads with” its own story, but the build puts the same six finance tiles at the top of all seven boards, and 05.1 describes exactly that strip. If the shared strip is intended, then five of those rows should read “what its board carries beneath the shared strip” — and the build passes six rows immediately. If the strip is not intended, the brand boards need reordering. That single decision moves six rows.

The evidence

Every screenshot below is the served page, taken at 1600 px wide by headless Chrome, at the byte-identical build named in the header.

Seven changes, and every fail is cleared

None of these is a rebuild. Five are a reorder or a single field; two are CSS.

  1. Put Founder Freedom back Three metrics already in the data, filtered out of the render. clears 02.1, 02.2
  2. Right-align the value in every tile One CSS rule — the unit is already attached. clears 03
  3. Two nav rows, picker into the header Four views on row one, three on row two; the month picker moves up one band. clears 01.4, 01.5, 01.6
  4. Lead each brand board with its own tiles The content is already built and sits below the shared strip. This is ordering only. clears 05.2 – 05.7
  5. Make NPS and cost belong to the department Right now seven numbers are pasted into eight tables. This is the only change on the list that needs new data, not new layout. clears 04.3, 04.4, 04.5
  6. Repoint four north stars ADM → department cost to serve; ITC → automation coverage (already a row in that table); BO 1 → on-time delivery; BO 2 → margin per site — and give BO 2 its own rows, not BO 1’s. clears 04.1
  7. Name the source on the tile, flag a stale reading, split closed from live Source is already in the library; it just needs to reach the tile. The other two need building. clears 07.1, 07.3, 07.4, and 01.3 with the source list in the banner

And one row needs a decision, not a fix

06.4 wants framework pillars on System, and 06.2 wants one honest metric count. Both are additions to the page rather than repairs: a pillars section, and a single number that agrees with itself.

Luke’s side — not scored, and here is why

The instruction was to score “your platform” and send back the fails. I could not get to it.

gsd.infinityapps.co.za answers with a Cloudflare Access wall for InfLegends: “Log in to gsd”, an email field and Send login code. The code is a one-time six-digit mail into your mailbox, so it stays yours — I do not type it and I do not ask for it. Two ways past it: you sign in and the score takes twenty minutes, or Luke scores his own platform against the same 33 rows and this document becomes the comparison.

What I did not do

Nothing was sent to Luke — no message, no mail. Nothing on the dashboard was changed, deployed or re-pointed, and no Zoho record was touched. This is a score of what is already served, and it is yours to send or to bin.
